L7@P0: Abstract. We present a method to construct a Ruelle–Pollicott spectrum for the geodesic flow on
L8@P0: manifolds with strictly negative curvature and a finite number of hyperbolic cusps.
L9@P0: Keywords. Ruelle–Pollicott resonances, hyperbolic cusps, b-calculus

L43@P1: Since this is where the “non-trivial” part of the dynamics happen, one can crucially use
L44@P1: Fredholm theory. In this paper, we consider a family of hyperbolic flows whose trapped set
L45@P1: is not compact. For this class, we explain how Ruelle–Pollicott resonances can be defined.
L46@P1: We are convinced that the methods developed in this article will also apply to more general
L47@P1: settings and that they will lead to subsequent results such as meromorphic continuation
L48@P1: of zeta functions, and decay of correlations results. However, the new arguments that we
L49@P1: introduce to handle the non-compact trapped set are already a bit more involved than the
L50@P1: usual ones. We have thus chosen to restrain ourselves to the following setting, where they
L51@P1: can be cleanly developed.

L103@P2: We now want to mention some results related to Theorem 1. In order to study eigenvalues of the Laplacian on moduli spaces, Avila and Gouëzel [1] develop a functional
L104@P2: analytic framework for the Teichmüller flows which are also a class of dynamical systems
L105@P2: with non-compact finite volume trapped set. They obtain a meromorphic continuation
L106@P2: of the resolvent to a neighbourhood of zero (cf. [1, Proposition 3.3]). It would probably be possible to adapt their method to geodesic flows on cusp manifolds in order to
L107@P2: obtain a continuation to a small strip along the imaginary axis (instead of C in our case).
L108@P2: However, their functional analytic tools are quite different from ours.
L109@P2: Another series of related results have been obtained for the special case of surfaces
L110@P2: of constant negative curvature with cusps. It has been shown in a series of articles by
L111@P2: Mayer, Morita and Pohl [41, 45, 49, 50] that one can associate the geodesic flow with
L112@P2: one-dimensional expanding maps, using a carefully chosen discretization. Out of this discretization, one can build transfer operators with discrete spectrum, and these spectra have
L113@P2: interesting relations to number theory and the theory of Maass cusp forms [7, 38, 43].
L114@P2: One should be able to recover these spectra as a subset2 of the resonances defined from
L115@P2: Theorem 1. It will be subject to further research to establish this connection precisely.
L116@P2: As Ruelle–Pollicott resonances are an important tool to study decay of correlations,
L117@P2: let us shortly mention that the question of mixing is not yet satisfactorily answered for our
L118@P2: class of cusp manifolds: for constant curvature manifolds with cusps, exponential decay
L119@P2: of correlations for the Liouville measure was proved in [44], while for variable curvature,
L120@P2: only its mixing property is known [12]. Two other recent results on the mixing of Weil–
L121@P2: Petersson geodesic flows on manifolds with cusp-like singularities3 have been obtained

L144@P3: Smale [58] raised the question if, for Axiom A flows, the Ruelle zeta function4 has a meromorphic continuation to C? This question has recently been affirmatively answered by
L145@P3: Dyatlov and Guillarmou [16] following a long series of precedent works that prove meromorphic continuation under additional assumptions [15, 17, 22, 23, 47, 52] (we refer to
L146@P3: [2,60] for a recent overview of the literature). In all the recent accounts [15–17,21,23] of
L147@P3: these meromorphically continued zeta functions, a meromorphically continued resolvent
L148@P3: was the central ingredient. Consequently, Theorem 1 indicates5that the Smale conjecture
L149@P3: could hold for geodesic flows on cusp manifolds, i.e. beyond the class of Axiom A flows.
L150@P3: So far, such a result is only known in the particular case of constant negative curvature
L151@P3: where it is a rather direct consequence of Selberg’s trace formula.
L152@P3: Contrary to the “classical” Ruelle–Pollicott resonances, the definition of “quantum”
L153@P3: resonances of the Laplace–Beltrami operator N on a cusp manifold N has been established for a long time starting with works of Maaß [40] and Selberg [56]. See the introduction of [37] for the constant curvature case, and [11, 46] for the variable curvature
L154@P3: case. In fact, the proof of our main result borrows ideas from the definition of quantum
L155@P3: resonances (such as the compact Sobolev embedding, Lemma 4.12).

L183@P4: Let us present the structure of the paper. In Section 1, we introduce the precise settings in which we are working and collect several properties of the geodesic flow on cusp
L184@P4: manifolds, that will be crucial in the sequel. To prove our theorem, we then build a first
L185@P4: parametrix in Section 2.2 following the arguments of [17,20]. The geometric construction
L186@P4: of the escape function is presented; however, the technical microlocal lemmas are proved
L187@P4: in Appendix A. Section 3 is devoted to introducing techniques adapted from b-calculus
L188@P4: and proving the meromorphic continuation of the resolvent of a certain class of translation invariant operators. These operators show up precisely when restricting the geodesic
L189@P4: flow to the zeroth Fourier mode in the cusp. In Section 4, such a resolvent is used for
L190@P4: the construction of a parametrix (up to compact remainder) of the geodesic flow vector
L191@P4: field. Then, using analytic Fredholm theory, we conclude on the meromorphic continuation announced in Theorem 1. In Sections 3 and 4, we work in a more general setting
L192@P4: under a list of assumptions. This should allow for an easy generalization to more general settings (such as fibred or complex hyperbolic cusps) in the future. In Section 5, we
L193@P4: finally compute explicitly the indicial roots for the b-operators associated to the geodesic
L194@P4: flow on our class of cusp manifolds and we check that all the necessary assumptions in
L195@P4: Section 3 and 4 are fulfilled.
L196@P4: Note that, in fact, we prove more general and more precise versions of Theorem 1.
L197@P4: For example, we continue the resolvent for a certain class of derivations on vector bundles
L198@P4: (cf. Definition 1.4) including the geodesic vector field with smooth potential, Lie derivatives on perpendicular k-forms and general associated vector bundles over constant
L199@P4: curvature manifolds (cf. Examples 1.5–1.7). Furthermore, we give a precise description of the wavefront set of the resolvent. For a full statement, we refer the reader to
L200@P4: Theorems 3 and 4.
